# MESA Trainings

> MESA Trainings: short, single-task tutorials for the MESA Portal at mesa.cyverse.org and its apps, written for training participants and for anyone using MESA. Each tutorial is one task in six fixed parts (what you will have, what you need, the steps, a check, the likely slip, what is next). Tutorials marked draft were written from the MESA documentation and have not been validated on the live portal. The source repository is an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) bundle: every page carries YAML frontmatter with type, provenance (generated/sources), and lifecycle (status/stale_after) fields.

Every page below is listed with three addresses that all return the same content: the rendered HTML page, its Markdown twin (page URL + `index.md`, served as text/markdown with the OKF frontmatter), and the raw source file on GitHub. Fetch whichever your tool is allowed to reach; many sandboxes permit github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com but not *.github.io.

```
Site page        https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/<path>/
Markdown twin    https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/<path>/index.md
Raw source       https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/<path>.md      (branch main; a moving target)

Content page     /tutorials/sign-in/  ->  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/sign-in.md
Section listing  /tutorials/          ->  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/index.md
```

The form https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/<path>.md also returns the same Markdown.

Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/index.md
- [Learning pathway](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/pathway/): The five points of the MESA learning pathway, from finding your way around to sharing work others can rerun, with the tutorials that belong to each. ## Tutorials

- [Sign in to the MESA Portal with a CyVerse account](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/sign-in/): Sign in to the MESA Portal at mesa.cyverse.org with a free CyVerse account and confirm that you reached your dashboard. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/sign-in/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/sign-in.md
- [Find MESA's community data in the Data Browser](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/find-community-data/): Open the MESA community folder in the portal's Data Browser, confirm where you are from the folder header, and copy a folder's path. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/find-community-data/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/find-community-data.md
- [Launch MESA JupyterLab with your Data Store mounted](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/launch-jupyterlab/): Start the MESA JupyterLab app from the MESA Portal and confirm that your CyVerse Data Store is available inside it. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/launch-jupyterlab/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/launch-jupyterlab.md
- [Save your work where it survives the session](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/save-your-work/): Save a notebook inside your Data Store from MESA JupyterLab and confirm from the MESA Portal that it will outlive the app. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/save-your-work/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/save-your-work.md
- [Stop an app and find your results](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/stop-app-find-results/): Stop a running MESA app with Save & Exit from the Analyses page and find its results in the Data Browser. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/stop-app-find-results/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/stop-app-find-results.md
- [Practice data: five invented rain gauges](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/practice-data/): The synthetic rain-gauge practice dataset used by the data tutorials: what its three files contain, its data dictionary, and how to copy it into your Data Store. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/practice-data/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/practice-data.md
- [Load a file from your Data Store into a notebook](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/load-a-file/): Read a CSV file that sits in your Data Store into a pandas table in MESA JupyterLab and confirm its size against what you expected. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/load-a-file/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/load-a-file.md
- [Read the data dictionary before the data](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/read-the-data-dictionary/): Use a dataset's data dictionary to find out what each column means and which column you cannot yet add up, before you compute anything. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/read-the-data-dictionary/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/read-the-data-dictionary.md
- [Check a column's range and missing values](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/check-range-and-missing/): Find the smallest and largest value in a column and count the blanks in every column, so that an impossible value or a gap shows up before you compute with it. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/check-range-and-missing/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/check-range-and-missing.md
- [Tally a quality flag before you trust a number](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/tally-a-quality-flag/): Count how many rows carry each value of a quality flag, including the blanks, and look at the flagged rows before deciding what to do with them. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/tally-a-quality-flag/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/tally-a-quality-flag.md
- [Count records per day to find incomplete days](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/count-records-per-day/): Count the rows for each gauge and day to find days that were recorded twice and days that were not recorded at all. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/count-records-per-day/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/count-records-per-day.md
- [Reconcile row counts before and after a join](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/reconcile-a-join/): Join a table of readings to a table of gauges and confirm that the join neither added nor lost rows and left no reading without a match. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/reconcile-a-join/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/reconcile-a-join.md
- [Leave a notebook someone else can rerun](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/leave-a-rerunnable-notebook/): Restart a notebook and run it from the top, remove what ties it to your session, and say at the top what it needs, so that another person gets the same result. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/leave-a-rerunnable-notebook/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/leave-a-rerunnable-notebook.md
- [Find your way around the MESA Portal](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/find-your-way-around/): Use the MESA Portal's sidebar, dashboard, and user menu to reach your data, the apps, your analyses, and your quota. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/find-your-way-around/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/find-your-way-around.md
- [Share a folder with a collaborator](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/share-a-folder/): Give one named CyVerse user read access to a folder in your Data Store from the MESA Portal's Data Browser, and confirm the access took effect. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/share-a-folder/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/share-a-folder.md
- [Add metadata to a file or folder](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/add-metadata/): Describe a folder in your Data Store with an attribute and a value from the MESA Portal's Data Browser, and confirm the description was saved. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/add-metadata/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/add-metadata.md
- [Sign in and start an AI agent in a MESA app](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/start-an-ai-agent/): Sign in to CyVerse from a terminal in a MESA app, connect an AI agent to a language model, and have it list the folders in your Data Store. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/start-an-ai-agent/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/start-an-ai-agent.md
- [Keep tokens and passwords out of saved files](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/keep-secrets-out-of-files/): Give a notebook a token without typing it into a cell, and confirm that the saved notebook does not contain it. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/keep-secrets-out-of-files/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/keep-secrets-out-of-files.md
- [Turn UTC timestamps into local days](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/local-days-from-utc/): Convert UTC timestamps to local time before grouping by day, and confirm the daily totals against values you already trust. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/local-days-from-utc/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/local-days-from-utc.md
- [Work with a long table, one row per kind of measurement](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/work-with-a-long-table/): Recognise a table that stacks several kinds of measurement in one value column, summarise each kind separately, and reshape it to one column per measurement. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/work-with-a-long-table/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/work-with-a-long-table.md
- [Query a Parquet file with DuckDB from a notebook](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/query-parquet-with-duckdb/): Run SQL against a Parquet file from a notebook with DuckDB, without loading the file into memory first, and bring a result back as a pandas table. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/query-parquet-with-duckdb/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/query-parquet-with-duckdb.md
- [Check an AI-suggested result against the data](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/check-a-suggested-result/): Test a result that an AI assistant, or anyone else, hands you: reproduce the number, find what it rests on, and say whether the claim survives. (draft) Markdown twin: https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/tutorials/check-a-suggested-result/index.md Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/idss-mesa/trainings/main/docs/tutorials/check-a-suggested-result.md

## Meta

- [Full corpus in one file](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/llms-full.txt): every page's Markdown with frontmatter, links made absolute; about 119 KB, roughly 31,000 tokens. Prefer it over fetching pages one at a time.
- [Update log](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/log/): dated history of changes to this bundle.
- [For AI agents](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/about/ai-agents/): endpoints, trust signals, and what to do if you cannot fetch this site.
- [Sitemap](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/sitemap.xml) and [robots.txt](https://idss-mesa.github.io/trainings/robots.txt): crawlers honour only the origin https://idss-mesa.github.io/robots.txt, which is equally permissive.
- [MESA project site](https://idss-mesa.github.io/llms.txt): origin-level llms.txt indexing the MESA site, the MESA documentation, and the MESA software repositories.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/idss-mesa/trainings): the bundle itself; `docs/` mirrors the site paths one to one.

These pages teach people to use the MESA Portal by hand. For how a feature works, read the MESA documentation at https://idss-mesa.github.io/docs/llms.txt; for CyVerse data itself, connect to the MESA MCP servers and call their tools.
